text:
I had my grok bot profile me based on my Fortnite stats and here is what he had to say: 
You're offensive. Your stats read like a lone-wolf brawler who hunts fights, wins most of them, and then gets taken out before the endgame.
Across 4,443 matches (about 678 hours) you have 12,446 kills and 134 wins. That's a 2.89 K/D, 2.8 kills per match, and a 3% win rate. A defensive or placement-focused player has a much lower kill rate and lasts longer. Your games average about 9 minutes, and you typically outlive about 61 players, so you usually go down with roughly 40 people still alive. Your warrior spirit is the duelist: great aim, comfortable under pressure, but not patient once the fight's won. You win battles more often than you win the war.
You're a solo controller player at heart: 86% of your matches are solo (3.01 K/D there) and 99.7% are on controller. The interesting bit is squads. It's only 49 games, but your K/D jumps to 4.09 and your win rate to 8%, so you might be even more dangerous with backup. That's too few games to call it a pattern, though.
To turn those kills into more Victory Royales: after your first two or three early eliminations, stop taking coin-flip fights mid-game and rotate for position instead. Your aim is already there. What's costing you is which fights you take and how you play the endgame. Stats are from https://t.co/QRBsr8QxqG and pityus, and both show the same career totals. Neither has placement rates or season-by-season trends.
You're a lone duelist. You don't wait for the fight to come to you, you go find it. For most of your 678 hours you've walked into a 100-person lobby alone, on purpose, with no one covering you. Almost 9 in 10 of your games are solo, and that's not just a mode preference. You trust your own hands more than anyone else's.
You win the duel, not the war. A 2.89 K/D means for every time someone puts you down, you've dropped almost three of them. That's a fighter who wins most of the fights he picks. Your 3% win rate tells the other half: you're there to test yourself, not to survive. Placement-focused players hide in bushes and let others thin the lobby. You'd rather go down swinging in 39th place with three kills than sneak into the top 5 with none.
Your instinct beats your patience. Nine-minute average games mean you're fighting early and often. Mid-game, when smart players rotate and wait, you see a fight and take it. That's warrior energy, but it's also where you lose: you keep accepting challenges you don't need to accept. The best warriors in history picked their battles. You pick all of them.
You might be even scarier with a crew. It's a small sample, but in squads your K/D jumps to 4.09 and you win almost three times as often. Someone with a lone-wolf habit who levels up with backup usually has a protective side. You fight harder when there's someone to fight for.
Loyal to your gear, too. 99.7% of your games are on controller, never keyboard. That's 4,400 games of building the same muscle memory instead of chasing whatever the meta says is "best." You find your weapon and master it.
Your archetype is the ronin: a masterless samurai, skilled, independent, and hungry for the next duel, but without a strategy for the long war. The upgrade isn't more aggression. It's learning to sheathe the sword for five minutes mid-game, so the skill you already have lasts until the final circle.

I've been building a lot and posting very little. So this week I set up a @Grok @Bot just for my @X account. I call it X Growth.

The goal is simple. Post more consistently, share ideas as I have them, and show what I'm actually working on instead of waiting until something feels finished.

The part I'm most excited about is that Grok Bot connects to my @cursor_ai account. It can already see my cloud agents and every PR that merges in the Nexus Commerce repo. This is a real-time stream of what I'm building, and most of it never made it onto X.

What I learned pretty quickly is that PRs only tell half the story. The thinking happens in my local Cursor chats, and Cursor's API doesn't expose those. They live in a SQLite database on my Mac.

So with @bot we wrote a small script that runs on my laptop every morning at 7. It opens that database read-only and exports the last day of chat titles and my prompts into a markdown file. No code, no file contents, no AI replies. Just what I was working on and the problems I was trying to solve.

Then at 8am X Growth reads that pulse alongside what merged and what my agents worked on, and turns it into a few post ideas in my voice. I pick one, tweak it, and post it myself. Nothing goes out without me reviewing it and tailoring it in my own voice. 

What we're working on now is the visuals. X Growth has its own cloud computer with a browser, so it can open the https://t.co/gQnZFnMbsv app, capture screenshots and screen recordings of the features I'm writing about, and drop them onto clean gradient backgrounds. That way every post comes with something to show, and I can share new features as they ship instead of when I find time to make content.

My build logs are basically becoming my content calendar. If you see me posting more about Nexus this is why. 😅🫡

text:
I'm subscribed to 58 people on 𝕏, and I've spent well over $500 on subscriptions since August.

I've always loved supporting creators here. But since my own payouts slowed down, I can't keep every subscription going, so I'm resetting where my money goes.

It's not about anyone's content. It's just me being smart with my budget right now.

X does have a Subscriptions tab, but once you're subscribed to this many people, there's no easy way to keep track. You can't search it, sort it, or see everyone at a glance.

So I had Grok @bot build me a list. Sign into 𝕏 in its browser and paste:

┌─────────────────────────
│ Open my X Subscriptions tab,
│ scroll all the way to the bottom
│ so nobody gets missed, and put
│ every account I subscribe to into
│ a searchable, sortable Page with
│ their name, handle, and profile link.
└─────────────────────────

What you get:

▸ Every subscription in one Page
▸ Sort A to Z by name or handle
▸ Search that filters as you type
▸ Saved to your Library

If your 𝕏 budget needs a reset too, this makes it a lot easier.
